They follow the prestigious Tokaido and try to make this journey as rich an experience as possible. They will pass through magnificent countryside, taste delicious culinary specialties, purchase souvenirs, benefit from the virtues of hot springs, and have unforgettable encounters. Playing the game The player whose Traveler is farthest behind on the road is the player who takes the next turn. This player must move their Traveler forward to the open space (dot) of their choice, freely passing over one or more open spaces. Once they have moved their Traveler, the player receives the benefit corresponding to this type of space. NOTE: Some of the spaces on the board are doubled. Double spaces are used only in games with 4 or 5 players. Description of the spaces (Standard Option for B ase Game / Additional Option for E xpansion Game) Encounters (Pink Locations) ( B ) The player draws one Encounter card and receives a bonus: Annaibito - Draw the indicated panorama, if completed draw a panorama of your choice. Kuge - Gain 3 coins. Miko - Add 1 point and 1 coin to the Temple (from the bank) Samurai - Gain 3 points. Shokunin - Draw a Souvenir card and score those points. New Encounters Promo Cards Itamae - Pay a coin to draw a meal card; add it if you don't already own it and score 6 points. Kitoushi - Pay a coin to choose a Panorama and score the corresponding points. Saru - Draw a Hot Spring card and score those points. Takuhatsuso - Pay a coin and score 4 points. ( E ) Pay 1 coin and select a Calligraphy card (counts for Chatterbox accomplishment) and gains end game bonuses: Contemplation - 3 points for each completed Panorama and 1 point per Cherry Tree. Fasting - Score 3 points for each uneaten meal at the Inn. Foresight - 2 points per coin. Nostalgia - 2 points for each Legendary Object and 1 point per Souvenir. Patience - Score 6 points if you are the last to arrive in the last Inn, otherwise score 2 points. Perfection - 2 points for each Accomplishment and 1 point for each Calligraphy card. Farm (Gold Locations) ( B ) The player earns 3 coins. ( E ) Player gambles 2 coins; (X= Loses coins, 1/2/3/3/4= Gains double that many coins). Hot Springs (Cyan/Light blue Locations) ( B ) The player takes a Hot Spring card. These cards are worth 2 or 3 points. ( E ) Pay 1 coin for a Bath House card worth 4 points (counts for Bather accomplishment). Panorama (Green/White/Sea Blue Locations) ( B ) There are three Panorama types and are made of 3 (Field), 4 (Mountain), or 5 (Sea) sections. When a player stops on a Panorama they take the first Panorama of that type that they do not have (value from 1-5) and scores that many points. Each traveler can create only a single panorama of each type and when completed can no longer stop on the spaces corresponding to that type. ( E ) A player may instead take a Cherry Tree and gain 2 points and 1 coin. [Rating: 1/10] I won't lie that I expected anything good from this game after reading Martin's [thread=874185]excellent review[/thread], but my experience confirms his points more or less exactly. As everything you do give you 2-3 points, I felt the game plays itself as most choices were obvious and the choice which mattered the most was which of 2 character to choose from before starting. So, it's a low interaction game, some tedious blocking, as samey as it gets, but with cutesy art which is abused for promoting such uninspired game. [Rating: 1/10] It's an activity, rather than a game. there are few meaningful decisions to be made. It's lovely to look at and an enjoyable family pastime, but not a game.

[Rating: 1/10] This is the only game that I can think of off the top of my head that I actively dislike and will refuse to play. For my kind of brain, it's hugely frustrating. You are expected to make decisions so I keep trying to calculate and optimize but there's no point - there are points for everything and tonnes of luck. Then, why make decisions at all? ...and yet the game still seems to want you to. I feel unwell when I play this game.

[Rating: 1/10] The components are beautiful, but this is not a game. I've heard that it's better with 2 players, but I've played this several times and none of the players did anything other than move to the first available slot. Preventing your opponents from taking multiple turns seemed to be a much stronger strategy than moving to the spot that would be best for you.

[Rating: 1/10] The popularity of this game is insulting. It is the 21st-century version of Candyland.

[Rating: 1/10] Quite a bit of complexity for not much game. There are way better gateway games out there, more engaging and that teach mechanics used in bigger games.

[Rating: 1/10] Fuck you the game, dont be fooled by the cute Japanese art this entire game is designed around running others life literally. Its the board game equivalent of musical chairs, how about instead of that you change the theme to the bloody violent side of Japanese history it would be more fitting at least be honest with what you were going for here mr game dev.

[Rating: 1/10] Nice theme and some good art.  Simple set collector with healthy dose of luck.  Most of the time it seems you just go to the next available space so the decision window is narrow.  My BGA game took 10 minutes and that felt long, cannot imagine this at 45 minutes.
